context: Sho asks Hina how long until kindergarten starts.

lines.speaker: sho_child
lines.en: Hina, how many more days until kindergarten?
lines.style: Soft, gentle inquiry. Quiet voice with genuine curiosity threading through. No hurry in the pace. Warm but understated — this is how Sho asks about things that matter to him.

lines.speaker: hina_child
lines.en: It's a long wait. Ten more days.
lines.style: Bright and matter-of-fact, counting it out with her fingers almost audibly. Genuinely pleased by the countdown itself. Warm, unselfconscious child-logic — the waiting is part of the fun.

lines.speaker: sho_child
lines.style: Quiet admission. Small voice but full of real feeling. Not performing excitement — this is genuine, understated longing. The kind of honest thing only a six-year-old says without embarrassment.

lines.speaker: hina_child
lines.en: We can count down together every day.
lines.style: Warm proposal, almost conspiratorial. She's offering him something — inclusion in her countdown. Bright without being loud. Generous in that unselfconscious way kids are when they like someone.

lines.speaker: sho_child
lines.en: Waiting is fun when we do it together.
lines.style: Quiet realization dawning in his voice. Soft, genuine warmth. Not a conclusion he's been told but one he's just arrived at. The small, satisfied tone of a shy child who feels understood.
